Andrea Adelson: Notre Dame. This team has veterans across the board and is motivated after the CFP snub last year.
Kyle Bonagura: Ohio State. The Buckeyes have a brutal schedule, but I think they'll silence the annual Texas offseason hype Sept. 12 and never look back.
Bill Connelly: Notre Dame. They have the perfect combination of talent, opportunity (read: navigable schedule) and a boulder-sized chip on their proverbial shoulder.
Heather Dinich: Texas. Nobody in the country has a more complete team in terms of roster and staff.
David Hale: Notre Dame. CJ Carr flashed signs of greatness last year. This is the season he puts it all together.
Eli Lederman: Notre Dame. Quarterback CJ Carr makes another jump, vaulting Notre Dame to its first title in 38 years.
Max Olson: Ohio State. This Buckeyes squad is loaded on offense, should have breakout stars on defense and will ultimately benefit in the CFP from facing so many tough tests.
Adam Rittenberg: Notre Dame. Carr is the type of quarterback Notre Dame hasn't had during its nearly four-decade drought without a national title.
Mark Schlabach: Ohio State. I've got to see the Longhorns do it, so I'm going with the Buckeyes despite their difficult schedule.
Jake Trotter: Texas. Transfer wideout Cam Coleman will help quarterback Arch Manning play at a championship level, and the Longhorns will claim their first title since 2005.
Paolo Uggetti: Oregon. This year — and this particular team — feels like a great opportunity.
Dave Wilson: Oregon. Dante Moore's return will power a dynamic offense, and a strong defensive front will hold up for the long-awaited breakthrough.
Chip Patterson: Ohio State. I'll take the battle-tested Buckeyes to put together another run for Ryan Day's second title in three years.
Brandon Marcello: Oregon. This is Lanning's best team yet in Eugene.
Brad Crawford: Notre Dame. Marcus Freeman's roster checks every box that matters in January.
Chris Hummer: Texas. This is the most talented Texas team since the mid-2000s when the Longhorns annually competed for championships.
Tom Fornelli: Indiana. This is still a very good team, and one that will certainly be tested during the regular season.
Andrea Adelson: Malachi Toney. The most dynamic player in college football will be lined up everywhere making plays for Miami.
Kyle Bonagura: Julian Sayin. Ohio State's QB finished fourth last year, and the only thing working against him is teammate Jeremiah Smith taking away votes.
Bill Connelly: Jeremiah Smith. It's hard for a receiver to coordinate all the votes, but Smith has an open lane.
Heather Dinich: Jeremiah Smith. It goes to the best player — not the best quarterback.
David Hale: CJ Carr. He's finally got some real talent to throw to, and Notre Dame is going to put up a lot of points.
Eli Lederman: Julian Sayin. Ohio State's junior QB turned in the third-most accurate season in FBS history as a first-year starter last fall.
Max Olson: CJ Carr. The ingredients are all there with his talent, supporting cast, defense and schedule.
Adam Rittenberg: Trinidad Chambliss. Arguably no quarterback was playing better at the end of last season.
Mark Schlabach: Julian Sayin. The Heisman Trophy typically goes to quarterbacks, and Sayin is who makes the Buckeyes' offense roll.
Jake Trotter: Jeremiah Smith. Shouldn't the Heisman go to the best player?
Paolo Uggetti: Dante Moore. If this is going to be Oregon's year, Moore has to be even better than he was last season.
Dave Wilson: Malachi Toney. We love flashy stars on big stages.
Chris Hummer: Darian Mensah. Miami stacks wins, Mensah throws for a lot of yards and he edges out some other quarterbacks.
Chip Patterson: CJ Carr. Carr is ready to be the most outstanding player in college football.
David Cobb: Arch Manning. No Manning has ever won the Heisman, but Arch will finally break the curse.
John Talty: Julian Sayin. If Sayin and Ohio State are as good as they are capable of being, he has as good a shot as anyone.
Brandon Marcello: Dante Moore. If his per-game average jumps while maintaining efficiency, Moore wins the Heisman.
